title: Flip leaky bucket into snap-through buckled nanobeam bit
idea: Worsen: store every bit in a leaky bucket that drains in milliseconds. Flip: store the bit in the shape of a pre-stressed buckled nanobeam (20 nm SiN or SiC) that snaps between two stable states under an electrostatic pulse and is read by the capacitance change to a sense electrode; a shape cannot leak.
why: Kills refresh (fact 3: 16-33% of idle power) and sidesteps the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); fJ-scale writes, unlimited retention, NEMS resonators already show >1e12 cycles.

title: Antiferroelectric charge-step capacitor that pins voltage against leakage
idea: Worsen: demand ever more charge from a linear dielectric, forcing AR 115:1 pillars. Flip: use an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich HZO film with the plate biased so a stored '1' sits just above the AFE-to-FE transition; the switching charge adds ~2-3x Q per area, and as leakage pulls the node down the film releases bound charge, creating a voltage plateau that stretches retention.
why: Fact 1 charge wall: the same Cs at AR ~25-30:1 instead of 60-75:1; the plateau effect could roughly double retention time (fact 3).

title: Topological polar vortex chirality as an unleakable bit
idea: Worsen: hold bits as fragile scalar charge that any trap can steal. Flip: encode the bit as the handedness (left or right chirality) of a polar vortex or polar skyrmion in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices, switched by a sub-volt field pulse with an in-plane bias and read by tunneling resistance or piezo-current; topology protects the state at ~10 nm size.
why: Density (sub-10 nm bits, no capacitor) and refresh elimination; the topological barrier gives non-volatility without diffusion-driven fatigue.

title: Antiferromagnet Neel-vector bit with zero stray field
idea: Worsen: use bits that disturb their neighbours (row hammer, stray fields) so cells must sit far apart. Flip: store the bit in the Neel vector of a chiral antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn or CuMnAs) switched by ns spin-orbit current pulses and read by anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance; antiferromagnets have no stray field and THz dynamics, so cells pack at minimum pitch and ignore neighbour activity.
why: Row-hammer immunity (fact 9), no refresh (fact 3), ps-ns writes; avoids the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM.

title: Erasable conducting domain wall in thin-film lithium niobate
idea: Worsen: read bits by dumping their charge onto a bitline, destroying them. Flip: store the bit as the presence or absence of a charged conducting domain wall in a thin-film LiNbO3 mesa between two electrodes; a field pulse injects or erases the wall, and a small read voltage senses its >1000x conductance without moving it.
why: Non-destructive read removes restore energy and the overfetch penalty (fact 8: 5.9 pJ per useful bit); current-mode sensing shrinks sense-amp area (fact 7).

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state as an electrons-only phase bit
idea: Worsen: store bits by moving atoms or ions, which wear out. Flip: store the bit in the electronic order of a charge-density-wave material (1T-TaS2) whose metastable 'hidden' metallic state is set by a ps current pulse and erased by a longer pulse; only electrons reorder, so there is no atomic wear, and resistance contrast is 10-100x.
why: Endurance and speed (ps writes, fJ energy) with non-volatility; attacks refresh and the voltage floor (facts 3, 10). Room-temperature stability is the open question.

title: Bits travel to the sensor: CMOS bucket-brigade loop memory
idea: Worsen: give every bit its own transistor, contact and wire so periphery and contacts eat the die. Flip: store bits as charge packets in buried-channel CCD potential wells clocked around short 256-bit loops with one sense and regeneration stage per loop; no per-cell transistor, contact or capacitor etch, so a cell is ~2-4F2 of gate electrodes.
why: Density and capital (no high-AR capacitor, fewer EUV contact layers, fact 4) and a smaller periphery share (fact 7); latency held under ~100 ns by many short parallel loops.

title: Silicon interband tunnel-diode latch cell needing no refresh
idea: Worsen: make the cell need constant topping-up at 1 V or more. Flip: tie the storage node to a pair of series Si/SiGe resonant interband tunnel diodes whose negative differential resistance creates two stable node voltages, so the cell self-latches at ~0.3 V with pA standby current (tunneling SRAM revived with CMOS-compatible diodes).
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth tax disappear (fact 3); a 3x lower operating voltage cuts CV2 energy ~9x (fact 10); about one transistor plus two diodes per cell.

title: Voltage-written multiferroic BiFeO3 bit with spin-orbit readout
idea: Worsen: write bits by pushing large currents or 3 V wordlines. Flip: store the bit in the coupled ferroelectric and antiferromagnetic order of a BiFeO3 film exchange-coupled to a CoFe nanomagnet, written by ~100 mV across the BFO and read by the inverse spin-Hall voltage in a topological-insulator strip (MESO-style physics used as a memory element).
why: aJ-fJ writes break the voltage floor (fact 10); non-volatility removes refresh (fact 3).

title: Quantum-paraelectric capacitor whose k explodes in cold pods
idea: Worsen: keep the dielectric constant fixed near 40 and keep etching deeper. Flip: run memory in 40-77 K pods and use quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 or KTaO3 as the cell dielectric, whose k climbs from ~300 to several thousand on cooling, so a planar or shallow-cup capacitor reaches 5 fF at 4F2.
why: Destroys the capacitor charge wall (fact 1: the k ~70 target exceeded >10x) and removes high-AR etch tools (capital, fact 4).

title: Electromechanical parametron: bit stored as oscillation phase
idea: Worsen: store bits as static levels that drift and leak. Flip: store each bit as the 0 or pi phase of a parametrically pumped high-Q NEMS resonator (Goto's parametron revived mechanically); the shared pump line continuously sustains whichever phase was seeded, so the state cannot leak away.
why: Replaces refresh with continuous low-power pumping (fact 3), needs no capacitor (fact 1), and phase coding is noise-robust so voltages can drop (fact 10).

title: NAND-style capacitor string sharing one transistor via threshold selectors
idea: Worsen: give each tiny capacitor its own expensive access transistor. Flip: stack 8-16 storage capacitors in a vertical string behind one access transistor, each gated by an ovonic threshold switch with staggered thresholds so the bitline voltage selects which capacitor charges or dumps.
why: 3D density without a lateral transistor per tier (fact 2); transistor count falls 8-16x and tiers are deposition-defined rather than litho-defined (fact 4).

title: Leakage-twinned differential cell where drain currents cancel
idea: Worsen: let each capacitor leak through its own random tail transistor. Flip: store the bit as the charge difference between two half-size capacitors sharing one split-fin access device and one junction, so the dominant leakage (GIDL, junction trap-assisted tunneling) drains both equally and the differential signal survives ~10x longer.
why: Attacks the retention tail (fact 3): refresh interval 5-10x longer; half-size caps offset the 2C area penalty.

title: Nanosecond protonic three-terminal bit with non-destructive channel read
idea: Worsen: use two-terminal cells where read and write fight over one path. Flip: store the bit as proton concentration in a 10 nm WO3 channel, moved through a phosphosilicate-glass electrolyte by ~5 ns gate pulses and read by channel conductance on a separate path at <0.1 V.
why: Non-volatile, non-destructive read (facts 3, 8) and sub-volt reads (fact 10); hydrogen is not a scarce resource.

title: Electrowetting nanodroplet that sits in one of two wells
idea: Worsen: hold bits with charge that escapes through any defect. Flip: seal a ~50 nm droplet of ionic liquid in a dumbbell cavity; an electrowetting pulse moves it to the left or right well, capillary pinning holds it there, and its position reads out as a capacitance difference.
why: Non-volatile and immune to leakage (fact 3), no high-k dielectric needed (fact 1); a fluid has no fatigue.

title: Metastable DX-centre traps with lattice-relaxation recapture barriers
idea: Worsen: trap charge behind thin barriers that tunneling defeats. Flip: store charge in an engineered layer of DX-like centres (Si-doped AlGaN or Ga2O3 defect complexes) whose large lattice relaxation creates a configurational barrier to recapture, giving persistent stored charge for hours at room temperature, written and erased by gate pulses.
why: Retention orders of magnitude beyond the 13 fA tail (fact 3) without a big capacitor (fact 1).

title: Deliberately imperfect bits: shorter capacitors for AI tensor mantissas
idea: Worsen: insist every bit of every byte meet 1e-15 error at worst-case retention. Flip: build a tolerant cell class with ~40% less capacitor height for neural-network weights and activations; sign and exponent bits live in full cells while low-order mantissa bits live in short cells refreshed rarely.
why: Cuts capacitor etch time, AR and refresh for the AI data that dominates demand (facts 1, 3, 4): ~20-30% lower cost per bit on that tier.

title: Laminated van der Waals capacitor stacks instead of deep etching
idea: Worsen: get capacitance only by etching 75:1 holes. Flip: build area by laminating 20-50 alternating graphene/hBN sheets into an interdigitated parallel-plate stack contacted on staircased edges, so capacitance scales with layer count rather than etch depth.
why: Avoids high-AR etch (fact 1) and tungsten fills; atomically flat hBN has very low leakage.

title: Vacuum-gap floating node written by field emission
idea: Worsen: store charge behind oxides whose traps leak and wear out. Flip: put the storage node on a nanoscale island isolated by a sealed 3-5 nm vacuum gap; writes use field emission across the gap, and retention relies on vacuum, which has no traps, no stress-induced leakage and no wear.
why: Removes the trap-assisted leakage tail (fact 3) and floating-gate endurance limits; a candidate refresh-free node.

title: Shadow-latch cell that hands its bit to a nonvolatile twin
idea: Worsen: keep refreshing billions of idle bits all night. Flip: pair each DRAM cell group with a tiny ferroelectric tunnel-junction shadow element; when a bank goes idle its bits are copied into the shadows in one burst, refresh stops, and the bits are restored on wake.
why: Idle refresh energy (16-33% of idle power, fact 3) drops to near zero while active speed stays DRAM-class.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina scaffold for litho-free capacitor arrays
idea: Worsen: pattern every capacitor hole with EUV and plasma etch. Flip: anodize an aluminium layer so it self-organizes into hexagonal 20-40 nm pores at >100:1 aspect ratio, ALD electrode/high-k/electrode inside the pores, and register access transistors to the natural lattice.
why: Removes litho and etch capital for the capacitor (fact 4) and reaches AR 115+ almost for free (fact 1).

title: Ferroelastic twin-domain bit read by piezoresistance
idea: Worsen: rely on polarization that fatigues as charged defects pile up. Flip: store the bit as the orientation of a ferroelastic twin domain (a strain state) in a nanopillar of a non-polar ferroelastic oxide, switched by a short strain pulse from an attached piezo film and read by orientation-dependent resistance.
why: Non-volatile with no free charge to leak (fact 3); potentially fatigue-free because no polar charge accumulates.

title: Nanopore electric double-layer capacitor with 100x areal capacitance
idea: Worsen: depend on solid dielectrics capped near k 40. Flip: fill shallow nanopores with an ionic-liquid or solid-electrolyte layer so the storage node is an electric double-layer capacitor (~10-20 uF/cm2, ~100x a 5 nm high-k film), with nm diffusion distances keeping charging near nanoseconds.
why: Breaks the capacitor charge wall without high AR (fact 1): planar 5 fF at <20 nm pitch.

title: FD-SOI buried-oxide back-gate cell on a 22nm shuttle
idea: Worsen: spend the whole budget inventing a capacitor process. Flip: on a ~$100k 22FDX multi-project wafer, use an isolated per-cell back-gate under the thin buried oxide as the storage node (the BOX is a free capacitor) and read the bit as a front-gate threshold shift; 24 months covers two tapeouts and retention characterization.
why: Proves a capacitor-free, non-destructive-read cell in a US-fab logic process; U.S. manufacturability with near-zero capital.

title: Nanoimprint-stamped capacitor pillar array instead of EUV
idea: Worsen: buy EUV exposures for every capacitor layer. Flip: because the capacitor array is a perfectly periodic hex lattice, write one master template by e-beam (~$150k) and replicate it by nanoimprint on a rented tool, demonstrating 30 nm-pitch capacitor holes on 200 mm test wafers within 18 months.
why: Capital and EUV intensity (fact 4): imprint is ~1/10 the cost per layer and removes the single-supplier EUV dependency for the storage array.

title: Fatigue-free sliding ferroelectric bilayers built by tear-and-stack
idea: Worsen: assume a new storage material needs a fab to evaluate. Flip: with a ~$300k glovebox and transfer stage, tear-and-stack parallel bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 whose polarization flips by interlayer sliding (no ion motion), and spend 24 months proving 1e12+ cycles and 10 ns switching on 100-device arrays.
why: An endurance-unlimited, atomically thin polarization bit (facts 1, 3); de-risks a new storage physics for under $1M.

title: Superconducting flux-trap cell taped out on an existing shuttle
idea: Worsen: assume new memory needs a new fab and billions. Flip: store bits as single flux quanta in kinetic-inductance NbN loops, taped out on an existing superconducting-electronics foundry shuttle (~$50-100k per run) and tested in a ~$250k cryocooler, targeting a 1e5-cell array for cryogenic AI datacentres.
why: aJ writes, zero static power, unlimited endurance (facts 3, 5, 10) with no new fab.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayers soaked into existing capacitor trenches
idea: Worsen: develop a deposition tool for a new dielectric. Flip: use wet chemistry to self-assemble redox-active porphyrin monolayers inside existing MIM or trench test capacitors so each molecule stores discrete electrons at fixed redox potentials; the budget is chemistry, a probe station and 24 months of cycling tests.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~2-5x charge per area, and discrete redox states could give 2 bits per cell; capital-free validation.

title: Chill commodity DDR5 to minus 40 C and stretch refresh
idea: Worsen: run memory hot beside 1 kW accelerators, where leakage doubles every ~10 C. Flip: build a $1M pilot of sealed two-phase-cooled DDR5 RDIMMs held at -40 C, where storage-node junction leakage drops ~100x, program the controller for 16x longer refresh intervals, and qualify within 24 months.
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth on existing chips right away (fact 3: recovers most of the 10-20% bandwidth tax).

title: Rescue reject-bin DRAM die by remapping only the weak cells
idea: Worsen: scrap dies because a few thousand storage cells leak too fast. Flip: buy fail-bin and downgraded dies cheaply, run a 24-month retention census on an FPGA tester to map weak cells, and ship modules whose controller remaps those cells or refreshes them more often.
why: Raises usable supply now; salvaged dies cost ~30-50% of new per bit, and the program needs ~$1M of capital.

title: Direct-tunnel germanium nanodot cell with seconds-long retention
idea: Worsen: force a choice between fast-but-leaky DRAM and slow-but-wearing flash. Flip: in a university cleanroom, grow Ge nanodots over a 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide on standard MOSFETs so electrons tunnel directly in ~10 ns (no hot carriers, no wear) and the Ge band offset holds them for seconds.
why: Refresh cut ~100x versus 64 ms (fact 3) with non-destructive read; ~$400k of fab time.

title: Charged microring junction: bits read by wavelength, not bitlines
idea: Worsen: read every bit through a long, power-hungry copper bitline. Flip: on a ~$60k silicon-photonics shuttle, store each bit as charge on the depletion capacitance of a microring's PN junction, which shifts its resonance, so one waveguide reads 32-64 bits in parallel by wavelength; demonstrated within 24 months.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5) and sense-amp periphery (fact 7), with optical readout next to the accelerator.

title: Sputtered AlScN ferroelectric cap with 20x hafnia's charge
idea: Worsen: depend on ALD precursors and hafnia wake-up cycling. Flip: use a used reactive-sputter tool (~$400k) to deposit 10 nm wurtzite AlScN on 200 mm CMOS back-end test chips and use its ~100 uC/cm2 polarization as a planar storage capacitor with no deep trench; 24 months maps endurance and scaling.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~20x charge per area versus a linear dielectric in a planar cap at low capital; endurance is the risk to retire.

title: Stiction-latched graphene nanorelay held by van der Waals force
idea: Worsen: hold the bit with a charge that leaks. Flip: hold it with adhesion: an exfoliated few-layer graphene cantilever snaps onto a contact and stays stuck by van der Waals force until a reverse pulse peels it off; build 100 devices in a university lab in 12 months and spend the next 12 on cycling.
why: Zero leakage, zero standby power, no refresh (fact 3), for under $500k.

title: Cloud DFT screen for a k-70 dielectric that ALD can grow
idea: Worsen: keep the k ~40 ZrO2 stack forever. Flip: spend ~$300k of cloud compute on a high-throughput DFT and phonon screen of rutile and alloyed oxides (Ti-Ge-Sn-O, Hf-Ti-O) for k >= 70 with band gap >= 4 eV and ALD growth below 450 C, then test the top five in a university ALD within 24 months.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): k 70 lets AR fall from 75:1 to ~45:1, a cheap route to a step change.

title: GaN polarization well that holds charge behind 3.4 eV walls
idea: Worsen: store charge in silicon, whose 1.1 eV gap invites thermal leakage. Flip: use a GaN-on-Si power-foundry shuttle (~$80k per run) to build AlGaN/GaN cells whose built-in polarization well stores electrons behind wide-bandgap barriers, aiming to show ~1000x lower leakage within 24 months.
why: Refresh (fact 3): hours of retention, using existing US and allied GaN fabs instead of DRAM fabs.

title: Bulk acoustic delay-line loop memory from RF filter fabs
idea: Worsen: build bits only in scarce DRAM fabs. Flip: store bits as acoustic pulses circulating in short AlN/ScAlN bulk-acoustic delay lines made by RF-filter foundries, with a CMOS regenerator per loop; a $1M, 24-month prototype targets 100 ns loops as a refresh-free buffer.
why: U.S. manufacturability (RF filter fabs are large and US-based), with no capacitor and no refresh; density is modest but capital is tiny.

title: Open-source DRAM-cell library on US foundry PDKs
idea: Worsen: keep storage-cell know-how locked inside three companies. Flip: spend $1M over 24 months designing, taping out and publishing open-source eDRAM and gain cells (thick-oxide 3T, MIM 1T1C) on SkyWater 130 and 22FDX PDKs with measured retention data, so any US chip team can add dense memory.
why: U.S. manufacturability and supply diversification; lowers the entry cost for new memory makers.

title: Repurpose LTPS display backplanes as giant 1T1C memory sheets
idea: Worsen: make memory only on 300 mm silicon at ~$10/cm2. Flip: an AMOLED backplane is already a 1T1C array, so re-mask an existing LTPS display line (3 um cells, storage caps, access TFTs) into memory sheets; $1M buys a re-spun driver IC and a 24-month cost-per-bit study for cold bulk-capacity tiers.
why: Capital and cost per area (~100x cheaper per cm2) using idle display-fab capacity; 100 ns-1 us latency fits a capacity tier.

title: Deep-trench storage caps from US trench-power MOSFET fabs
idea: Worsen: claim only DRAM fabs can etch high-AR capacitors. Flip: trench-MOSFET power fabs (mature 200 mm, US-based) already etch deep silicon trenches daily; fund ~$700k of engineering lots to make 40:1 trench capacitors at 200 nm pitch as the storage layer of a 3D-bonded memory die.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: depreciated 200 mm tools, and IBM eDRAM already proved trench storage caps.

title: High-pressure deuterium anneal to harden storage-node junctions
idea: Worsen: leave hydrogen-passivated interface traps that de-passivate and feed the leakage tail. Flip: replace the final forming-gas anneal with high-pressure deuterium, whose heavier isotope bonds resist hot-carrier and thermal de-passivation (the giant isotope effect), and test tail retention on purchased DRAM test wafers within 24 months.
why: Fact 3 leakage tail: if the worst 0.01% of cells improve 2-4x, refresh interval doubles, from a cheap drop-in process change.

title: One-million-dollar Bit Prize judged on a standard test chip
idea: Worsen: let only incumbents with billion-dollar fabs propose storage elements. Flip: put the full $1M into a 24-month open prize: any storage element that hits 20 ns write, 1e15 cycles and 1 s retention on a supplied standard probe-card test vehicle wins, judged on measured data.
why: Leverages ~10-100x the budget in outside R&D effort and surfaces new storage physics fast.

title: Leakage-balanced loadless node that holds its own bit
idea: Worsen: let leakage only ever drain the storage node toward zero. Flip: design a 4T loadless cell on a ~$50k shuttle where the access transistors' off-current deliberately trickles charge into the high node while cross-coupled pull-downs sink the low node, so leakage itself holds the bit.
why: Eliminates refresh (fact 3) with 4 transistors instead of 6T SRAM and no capacitor; cheap to prove within 24 months.

title: Image-sensor pinned photodiode as an ultra-low-leakage storage well
idea: Worsen: store charge right at a trap-filled Si/SiO2 surface. Flip: a CMOS image sensor's pinned photodiode buries charge in a fully depleted well with ~1 e-/s dark current and lossless charge transfer; spend 24 months running blacked-out commercial sensors as memories, then a CIS-foundry shuttle for a compact 'dark pixel' memory cell.
why: Leakage ~1e4 below DRAM (fact 3), using the large CIS fab base instead of DRAM capacity.

title: Alpha-In2Se3 ferroelectric-semiconductor channel storing bits in-channel
idea: Worsen: need a separate capacitor plus a transistor for every bit. Flip: CVD-grow alpha-In2Se3, a 2D semiconductor that is itself ferroelectric, so the channel's own polarization sets its conductance (one device gives storage plus read gain); a $600k university program demonstrates 100-device arrays and 10 ns writes within 24 months.
why: Charge wall (fact 1) and transistor count, with non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: Colloidal BaTiO3 nanocube dielectric poured into capacitor wells
idea: Worsen: make a k ~70 dielectric only by atom-by-atom ALD. Flip: borrow the MLCC industry's BaTiO3 nanocube powders, spin-cast self-assembled 10-20 nm cubes into shallow capacitor wells and infiltrate them with ALD alumina, aiming at effective k of 100-300 in a $1M, 24-month bench program.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): AR could drop to ~20:1, with low capital and an existing MLCC supply chain.
